title: What to watch at the open
text: Stocks rose on Tuesday. The Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ gained 0.6% to $685.28 and the S&P 500 fund SPY gained 0.3% to $754.35. After the close, AMD shared its third quarter results. A search of the company filing summary says sales were $13.4 billion, above the $13 billion the company had guided. This morning, watch how AMD and other chip stocks trade in the first minutes, because one company's report can move its whole industry. A big first move is not always the final move, so patience is a skill.

title: AMD reported sales above its own guide
text: AMD closed at $483.90 on Tuesday, up 3.7%, before its report. Guidance means the company's own forecast. The company had forecast about $13 billion in sales for the quarter, and a filing summary reports $13.4 billion. We could not open the full report, so details such as next quarter's outlook are not confirmed here. Stocks can still fall on good news if people hoped for even more.

title: Industrial companies led the Nasdaq sectors
text: Among Nasdaq companies, industrials rose about 1.7%, real estate 1.5%, utilities 1.2% and technology 0.8%. Basic materials fell 1.5% and consumer defensive firms (stores that sell everyday goods) fell 1.2%. A sector is a group of companies in the same kind of business. Seeing which groups lead helps you understand the market's mood.

title: Bond yields stay high as the Treasury plans its borrowing
text: The 10 year Treasury yield, the interest the government pays to borrow for ten years, averaged 5.13% in October, the highest of the last 12 months. The Treasury is also set to say today how much it plans to borrow. When safe bonds pay more, growth stocks can feel pressure because investors have a tempting alternative.

title: Calmer funds lagged the rebound
text: The dividend fund SCHD fell 1.0% to $35.55 and Lockheed Martin fell 0.6% to $639.00 while fast growing companies like Vertiv (up 5.2%) and Rocket Lab (up 4.5%) jumped. Steadier names tend to move less on big days in both directions.

title: Lesson 36: What is trading volume?
text: Volume is the number of shares that change hands in a day. Think of a school cafeteria: a busy lunch line means many people are buying, and an empty one means few. On Tuesday about 90 million NVIDIA shares traded, while the usual day is closer to 120 million. High volume on a big price move suggests many people agree with the move. A big move on very low volume can be less reliable, because only a few trades pushed the price. Volume is a clue, not a promise. This is education, not advice.

title: Data coverage
text: Prices and ranges come from FMP for all 17 names, as of Tuesday's close. Analyst price targets, P/E and debt numbers were refreshed for NVDA, TSM, AMD, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META and GE, and Lockheed Martin has a target. AVGO, VRT, RKLB, LLY and ISRG have no free analyst data, so those cells stay empty. AMD's report numbers come from a search summary of the company filing, not the full document.
